newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bids drop to $62.50 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bids drop to $62.50 -feedlots.

text.p: Meat packers reduced bids for fed cattle in U.S. Plains feedlot markets to $62.00 to $62.50 per cwt after active trading early Tuesday at $63.00, feedlot sources said.

Feedlot sources from the Texas Panhandle to southwest Kansas reported a large number of cattle traded at $63.00 early Tuesday. Later in the morning, bids dropped to $62.00 and $62.50 but were largely passed by feedlots.
"This morning's trade was really rapid," said a Kansas cattle feeder of the $63.00 sales. He said he'd sold 700 head of mostly steers weighing 1,200 to 1,225 lbs at $63.00.
At $63.00 feedlots probably covered costs on cattle placed in feedlots as young calves, but lost $10 to $35 per head on cattle placed on feed as yearlings, sources said.
Cattle feeders said most of Tuesday's sales probably will not be shipped until next week because packers have yet to take delivery of cattle bought last week.
